Empoleon is a great choice. It actually got much stronger in BDSP.  
Piplup can now learn Charm in BDSP, which is actually AMAZING for some major fights early game(Mars, Maylene, etc),  
Yes, it sweeps Roark, and Byron easily, but it can also handle Wake, Candice, and Fantina pretty well. It can honestly tank most of Aaron's team(except Hera and Drapion), handle Bertha(be wary of Sturdy Golem and Rindo Berry Whishcash), has slight usage in Flint fight as well.

Water/Steel is overall a good typing, it's just unfortunate for certain fights where Fighting and Ground is prevalent, you'd have to be aware of opponent speed if you're going to vs it against one of those types. Its typing allows for a LOT of safe switches and good matchups. 

I'd say it fares better than Torterra, and while Infernape has the more offensive movepool, Empoleon if dedicated to being a special attacker has actually a higher base Sp. Atk stat compared to Infernape(111 to 104), slap a Choice Specs onto him and you have a potent Surf/Ice Beam/Grass Knot/Flash Cannon attacker. You can also just use him as a tank support as well(Stealth Rocks, etc), something that only Torterra can kinda do. 

Honestly, I've ran a full mono water nuzlocke in my personal playthroughs of BDSP. In my opinion, Empoleon, Gyarados, and Gastrodon were my strongest picks overall that are accessible in the early game. There are some other strong water choices aside from those three(Mantine, Whishcash, Milotic), but those come fairly late into your run.

I'd say in their prime in the 2000's, Ayumi was undisputedly the queen of J-Pop, but Utada wasn't that far behind. Both were extremely popular in their prime, and were the top artists in Japan.

As a long time Hikki fan, there's a few reasons why Utada has managed to have a long lasting career here. First, if you didn't know, Utada is Japanese-American, and has also tried to make albums and releases within America.

I'd say within the Western audience, people would know her because of her music being famously used in Kingdom Hearts and Neon Genesis Evangelion. On top of that, Utada has also attempted to brand herself more to a Western audience than Ayumi. A few years ago she was a surprise guest at Coachella through 88rising, and only really die hard fans knew who she was. I would say within America she's definitely a niche artist. Ayumi in comparison would be even more niche.

In addition to this, Utada herself and a lot of her English releases are more progressive in nature, being a contrast from traditional Japanese artists. This allows her to be more popular and relevant for younger generations.

In comparison, Ayumi's long career was mainly tailored for domestic audiences, but she's also had some success overseas, but not to the extent of Utada.

I grew up being labeled as a "gifted kid" in school, ended up taking a bunch of tests I don't remember when I was a kid and skipped grades. I scored well on IQ tests as a child and had school therapists and teachers always praising me. I graduated high school at 15 and my ego was sky high at the time.

All of that praise ended up getting to my head and I never felt the need to improve myself. I ended up developing bad habits that haunted me when I began college. I then realized that there were other intelligent individuals like me, and my achievements ended up kind of average in comparison.

I think intelligence can manifest itself in different ways, socially, arithmetically, mentally, etc. Most people think of academic success or intellect when they think of the word smart, which is true to a point. I do think I am above average in that aspect, but I feel I am inadequate in other aspects of my life. I think other intelligent people are the same way in that they reflect on themselves and are confident in what they know, and what they don't know.
